Please welcome Sean Malcolm, a seasoned tennis coach with 18 years of experience fostering player development and well-being. With a bachelor's in sports science and a master's in sports psychology from Laubara University, Sean is now pursuing a PhD in coaching and skill acquisition. Today he'll be presenting using the Constraints Let approach to design activities for beginner players, offering insights into effective, adaptable methods for early skill development. Let's give a warm welcome to Sean. At the start of London, UK, I run a tennis program called Infinite Tennis and recently I've embarked on a PhD program with Keith Davids based out of Sheffield-Hallam University. Very excited to share some content today around this theme of using the Constraints Let approach to design activities for beginner players. This content is the beginning of a research project where I'll be researching the coach experience of using the content and trying to develop their practice in this way. The group of players that we used for this project, some of them had never played tennis before. This was their first experience and others were a little bit more experienced, but still at the beginner level. Okay, for this project we started with the FEDAL LTA Youth Principles, which have been in place for a few years now. They were developed in collaboration with Loughborough University and 60-plus leading
